title.zh: 卷五十六 志第二十五: 儀衞志二
title.raw: 卷五十六 志第二十五: 儀衞志二 Volume 56 Treatises 26: Ceremonial Guards 2

sentences.zh: 儀衛誌二 ○國服

translations.literal: Ceremonial Guards, Part 2 ○ National Dress
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Guards, Part 2 — National Dress

sentences.zh: 上古之人，網罟禽獸，食肉衣皮，以儷鹿韋掩前後，謂之鞸。

translations.literal: The people of high antiquity caught beasts with nets, ate meat and wore hides, covering front and back with paired deer leather—called bian.
translations.idiomatic: In high antiquity, people hunted game with nets, ate meat and wore hides, and covered themselves front and back with paired deer hides—this was called the bian apron.

sentences.zh: 然後夏葛冬裘之制興焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter the system of summer ramie and winter fur arose.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the custom of ramie in summer and furs in winter take shape.

sentences.zh: 周公陳王業，《七月》之詩，至於一日於貉，三月條桑，八月載績，公私之用由是出矣。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou expounded the royal enterprise; the "Seventh Month" poem goes so far as one day hunting badgers, third month trimming mulberry, eighth month carrying the spun work—public and private uses issued from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou set forth the royal enterprise, and in the "Seventh Month" ode one finds a day spent hunting badgers, the third month devoted to tending mulberry, and the eighth month bearing home the spun cloth—thus arose what supplied both public and private needs.

sentences.zh: 契丹轉居薦草之間，去邃古之風猶未遠也。

translations.literal: The Khitan moved about among saltwort grass; they were still not far from deep-ancient customs.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan roamed among saltwort pastures, and customs of the deep past were still close at hand.

sentences.zh: 太祖仲父述瀾，以遙輦氏於越之官，占居潢河沃壤，始置城邑，為樹藝、桑麻、組織之教，有遼王業之隆，其亦肇跡於此乎！

translations.literal: Taizu's father's younger brother Shulü, holding the Yaonian clan office of yuyue, occupied the fertile banks of the Huang River, first established walled settlements, and instituted instruction in planting, mulberry and hemp, and weaving—the rise of the Liao royal enterprise perhaps also took its first traces here!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu's uncle Shulü, who held the office of yuyue in the Yaonian clan, settled on the fertile banks of the Huang River, founded the first walled towns, and introduced agriculture, sericulture, and weaving. The grandeur of the Liao royal enterprise may well have begun here.

sentences.zh: 太祖帝北方，太宗制中國，紫銀之鼠，羅綺之篚，麇載而至。

translations.literal: Taizu became emperor of the north; Taizong ruled China. Purple-silver sable, baskets of gauze and silk—herds of loads arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu reigned over the north, and Emperor Taizong governed China; purple-silver sable and baskets of gauze and brocade arrived in train upon train.

sentences.zh: 纖麗耎毳，被土綢木。

translations.literal: Fine, beautiful, soft furs covered the land like silk over trees.
translations.idiomatic: Fine, lustrous, and soft furs spread over the land as silk might cover trees.

sentences.zh: 於是定衣冠之制，北班國制，南班漢制，各從其便焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon hat-and-robe regulations were fixed: the northern bureau used national dress, the southern bureau Han dress—each following what was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for caps and robes were then established: the northern court followed Khitan national dress and the southern court Chinese dress, each according to its own usage.

sentences.zh: 詳國服以著厥始雲。

translations.literal: National dress is set forth in detail to record its beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: National dress is described in detail here to record how it began.

sentences.zh: 祭服：遼國以祭山為大禮，服飾尤盛。

translations.literal: Sacrificial dress: the Liao state regarded mountain sacrifice as the great rite; attire was especially elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial dress: the Liao regarded mountain sacrifice as their greatest ritual, and the ceremonial attire was especially magnificent.

sentences.zh: 大祀，皇帝服金文金冠，白綾袍，紅帶，懸魚，三山紅垂。

translations.literal: For great sacrifices, the emperor wore a gold-inscribed gold crown, white gauze robe, red belt, suspended fish pendant, and three-peaked red pendants.
translations.idiomatic: At great sacrifices the emperor wore a gold crown inscribed with gold patterns, a white gauze robe, a red belt, a suspended fish pendant, and three-peaked red streamers.

sentences.zh: 飾犀玉刀錯，絡縫烏靴。

translations.literal: He adorned himself with rhinoceros-horn and jade knife fittings and wore black boots with stitched trim.
translations.idiomatic: He wore rhinoceros-horn and jade knife ornaments and black boots with ornamental stitching.

sentences.zh: 小祀，皇帝硬帽，紅克絲龜文袍。

translations.literal: For minor sacrifices, the emperor wore a stiff cap and a red ke-si robe with tortoise patterns.
translations.idiomatic: At minor sacrifices the emperor wore a stiff cap and a red ke-si robe patterned with tortoises.

sentences.zh: 皇后戴紅帕，服絡縫紅袍，懸玉佩，雙同心帕，絡縫烏靴。

translations.literal: The empress wore a red kerchief, a red robe with stitched trim, suspended jade pendants, paired concentric kerchiefs, and black boots with stitched trim.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wore a red kerchief, a red robe with ornamental stitching, suspended jade pendants, paired concentric kerchiefs, and black boots with ornamental stitching.

sentences.zh: 臣僚、命婦服飾，各從本部旗幟之色。

translations.literal: Officials and titled ladies followed the colors of their own bureau's banners and standards.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and ennobled ladies dressed in colors matching the banners of their respective bureaus.

sentences.zh: 朝服：太祖丙寅歲即皇帝位，朝服衷甲，以備非常。

translations.literal: Court dress: in the bingyin year Taizu ascended the throne; court dress was worn over armor within, to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress: when Emperor Taizu took the throne in the bingyin year, he wore court robes over hidden armor as a precaution against emergencies.

sentences.zh: 其後行瑟瑟禮、大射柳，即此服。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when performing the sese rite and great willow-shooting, this was the dress worn.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter this was the dress worn for the sese rite and the great willow-shooting ceremony.

sentences.zh: 聖宗統和元年冊承天皇太后，給三品以上用漢法服，三品以下用大射柳之服。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tonghe, when Shengzong invested Empress Dowager Chengtian, officials of third rank and above were given Han-style court robes, and those below third rank the great willow-shooting dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tonghe, when Emperor Shengzong invested Empress Dowager Chengtian, officials of third rank and above received Chinese court robes and those below third rank the great willow-shooting dress.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服實裏薛袞冠，絡縫紅袍，垂飾犀玉帶錯，絡縫靴，謂之國服袞冕。

translations.literal: The emperor wore the shili xuegun crown, a red robe with stitched trim, hanging rhinoceros-horn and jade belt fittings, and stitched boots—called the national dress of full regalia.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore the shili xuegun crown, a red robe with ornamental stitching, rhinoceros-horn and jade belt ornaments, and ornamented boots—this was called the national full regalia.

sentences.zh: 太宗更以錦袍、金帶。

translations.literal: Taizong further changed to brocade robe and gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong later substituted a brocade robe and gold belt.

sentences.zh: 臣僚戴氈冠，金花為飾，或加珠玉翠毛，額後垂金花，織成夾帶，中貯發一總。

translations.literal: Officials wore felt caps adorned with gold flowers, sometimes adding pearls, jade, and kingfisher feathers; gold flowers hung behind the forehead; woven double belts held a lock of hair within.
translations.idiomatic: Officials wore felt caps decorated with gold flowers, sometimes augmented with pearls, jade, and kingfisher feathers, with gold flowers hanging behind the brow; woven double belts held a lock of hair inside.

sentences.zh: 或紗冠，制如烏紗帽，無檐，不擫雙耳。

translations.literal: Or they wore gauze caps fashioned like black gauze hats, without brims and without folding down the side flaps.
translations.idiomatic: Some wore gauze caps modeled on the black gauze official hat, brimless and without folded side flaps.

sentences.zh: 額前綴金花，上結紫帶。

translations.literal: Gold flowers were affixed before the forehead, with a purple band tied above.
translations.idiomatic: Gold flowers were fixed before the brow, with a purple band tied above.

sentences.zh: 末綴珠。

translations.literal: Pearls were attached at the ends.
translations.idiomatic: Pearls hung from the ends.

sentences.zh: 服紫窄袍、系䩞鞢帶，以黃紅色絳裹革為之，用金玉、水晶、靛石綴飾，謂之「盤紫」。

translations.literal: They wore narrow purple robes and fastened xiedie belts made of yellow-red silk-wrapped leather, adorned with gold, jade, crystal, and lapis—called "panzi."
translations.idiomatic: They wore narrow purple robes and fastened xiedie belts of yellow-red silk-wrapped leather ornamented with gold, jade, crystal, and lapis lazuli—this ensemble was called "panzi."

sentences.zh: 太宗更以錦袍、金帶。

translations.literal: Taizong further changed to brocade robe and gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong later substituted a brocade robe and gold belt.

sentences.zh: 會同元年，群臣高年有爵秩者，皆賜之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huitong, all ministers of advanced age who held noble ranks were granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huitong, all ministers of advanced age who held noble ranks were granted this dress.

sentences.zh: 公服：謂之「展裹」，著紫。

translations.literal: Official dress: called "zhan guo," worn in purple.
translations.idiomatic: Official dress, called "zhan guo," was worn in purple.

sentences.zh: 興宗重熙二十二年，詔八房族巾幘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Chongxi, Xingzong ordered the eight house clans to wear headcloths and caps.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Chongxi, Emperor Xingzong ordered the eight house clans to wear headcloths and caps.

sentences.zh: 道宗清寧元年，詔非勛戚之後及夷離堇副使並承應有職事人，不帶巾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingning, Daozong ordered that those who were not descendants of meritorious kin, nor deputy yilijin, nor attendants with official duties, were not to wear the headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingning, Emperor Daozong decreed that only descendants of meritorious families, deputy yilijin, and attendants holding official posts might wear the headcloth.

sentences.zh: 皇帝紫皂幅巾，紫窄袍，玉束帶，或衣紅襖；

translations.literal: The emperor wore a purple-black wrapped headcloth, narrow purple robe, jade girdle, or sometimes a red jacket;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore a purple-black wrapped headcloth, a narrow purple robe, and a jade girdle, or sometimes a red jacket;

sentences.zh: 臣僚亦幅巾，紫衣。

translations.literal: Officials likewise wore wrapped headcloths and purple garments.
translations.idiomatic: Officials likewise wore wrapped headcloths and purple garments.

sentences.zh: 常服：

translations.literal: Ordinary dress:
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary dress:

sentences.zh: 《宰相中謝儀》，帝常服。

translations.literal: In the "Rite of the Chancellor's Mid-Audience Thanks," the emperor wore ordinary dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rite of the Chancellor's Mid-Audience Thanks, the emperor wore ordinary dress.

sentences.zh: 《高麗使入見儀》，臣僚便衣，謂之「盤裹」。

translations.literal: In the "Rite of the Goryeo Envoy's Audience," officials wore informal dress, called "pan guo."
translations.idiomatic: In the Rite of the Goryeo Envoy's Audience, officials wore informal dress called "pan guo."

sentences.zh: 綠花窄袍，中單多紅綠色。

translations.literal: Green floral narrow robes; undergarments mostly red and green.
translations.idiomatic: They wore narrow robes with green floral patterns and undergarments mostly in red and green.

sentences.zh: 貴者披貂裘，以紫黑色為貴，青次之。

translations.literal: The noble wore sable furs; purple-black was most esteemed, blue next.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy wore sable cloaks; purple-black was most prized, blue next in rank.

sentences.zh: 又有銀鼠，尤潔白。

translations.literal: There was also silver sable, especially pure white.
translations.idiomatic: There was also silver sable, prized for its exceptional whiteness.

sentences.zh: 賤者貂毛、羊、鼠、沙狐裘。

translations.literal: The lowly wore sable hair, sheep, rat, and sand-fox furs.
translations.idiomatic: Those of lower rank wore sable hair, sheep, rat, and sand-fox furs.

sentences.zh: 田獵服：

translations.literal: Hunting dress:
translations.idiomatic: Hunting dress:

sentences.zh: 皇帝幅巾，擐甲戎裝，以貂鼠或鵝項、鴨頭為扞腰。

translations.literal: The emperor wore a wrapped headcloth and donned armor in martial dress, using sable or goose-neck or duck-head pieces as waist guards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore a wrapped headcloth and martial armor, with sable, goose-neck, or duck-head pieces as waist guards.

sentences.zh: 蕃漢諸司使以上並戎裝，衣皆左衽，黑綠色。

translations.literal: Khitan and Han commissioners of the various bureaus and above all wore martial dress; garments were all left-lapped, black-green in color.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan and Han commissioners of the various bureaus and above all wore martial dress with left-lapped garments in black-green.

sentences.zh: 吊服：太祖叛弟剌哥等降，素服受之。

translations.literal: Mourning dress: when Taizu's rebel younger brother Cige and others surrendered, he received them in plain white dress.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning dress: when Emperor Taizu's rebel younger brother Cige and others surrendered, he received them in plain white dress.

sentences.zh: 素服，乘赭白馬。

translations.literal: Plain white dress, riding a reddish-white horse.
translations.idiomatic: He wore plain white dress and rode a reddish-white horse.

sentences.zh: 祭服：終遼之世，郊丘不建，大裘冕服不書。

translations.literal: Sacrificial dress: throughout the Liao, suburban altars were not established, and the great fur robe and full regalia are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial dress: throughout the Liao dynasty suburban altars were never established, and the great fur robe and full regalia are not described here.

sentences.zh: 袞冕，祭祀宗廟、遣上將出征、飲至、踐阼、加元服、納後若元日受朝則服之。

translations.literal: Full regalia was worn for sacrifices to the ancestral temple, dispatching great generals on campaign, victory banquets, ascending the throne, coming-of-age, receiving an empress, and receiving court on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: Full regalia was worn for sacrifices at the ancestral temple, dispatching great generals on campaign, victory banquets, ascending the throne, coming-of-age ceremonies, receiving an empress, and the New Year's court audience.

sentences.zh: 金飾，垂白珠十二旒，以組為纓，色如其綬，黈纊充耳，玉簪導。

translations.literal: Gold ornaments; twelve strings of white pearls hung down; silk cords served as tassels, colored like the sash; yellow silk filled the ears; jade hairpins guided the crown.
translations.idiomatic: It was adorned with gold; twelve strings of white pearls hung down; silk cords served as tassels matching the sash in color; yellow silk filled the ears; and jade hairpins secured the crown.

sentences.zh: 玄衣、纁裳十二章：八章在衣，日、月、星、龍、華蟲、火、山、宗彜；

translations.literal: Black upper garment and vermilion lower garment with twelve emblems: eight on the robe—sun, moon, stars, dragon, flowering creatures, fire, mountain, and ritual vessels;
translations.idiomatic: The black upper robe and vermilion lower skirt bore twelve emblems: eight on the robe—the sun, moon, stars, dragon, flowering creatures, fire, mountain, and ritual vessels;

sentences.zh: 四章在裳，藻、粉米、黼、黻。

translations.literal: four on the skirt—waterweed, grain, axe-head, and opposed squares.
translations.idiomatic: four on the skirt—waterweed, grain, axe-head pattern, and opposed squares.

sentences.zh: 衣褾領，為升龍織成文，各為六等。

translations.literal: The robe collar and lapel were woven with ascending dragons in six grades.
translations.idiomatic: The collar and lapel were woven with ascending dragons in six grades.

sentences.zh: 龍山以下，每章一行，行十二，白紗中單，黼領，青褾襈裾，黼革帶、大帶，劍佩綬，舄加金飾。

translations.literal: Below dragon and mountain, each emblem occupied one row of twelve; white gauze undergarment, axe-pattern collar, blue lapel and vermilion skirt hem, axe-pattern leather belt and great belt, sword, pendant sash, and shoes with gold ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Below the dragon and mountain emblems, each symbol occupied one row of twelve; there was a white gauze undergarment, an axe-pattern collar, blue lapel and vermilion skirt hem, axe-pattern leather and great belts, sword, pendant sash, and gold-adorned shoes.

sentences.zh: 《元日朝會儀》，皇帝服袞冕。

translations.literal: In the "New Year's Court Assembly Rite," the emperor wore full regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rite of the New Year's Court Assembly, the emperor wore full regalia.

sentences.zh: 朝服：乾亨五年，聖宗冊承天太后，給三品以上法服。

translations.literal: Court dress: in the fifth year of Qianheng, when Shengzong invested Empress Dowager Chengtian, officials of third rank and above were given court robes.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress: in the fifth year of Qianheng, when Emperor Shengzong invested Empress Dowager Chengtian, officials of third rank and above received formal court robes.

sentences.zh: 《雜禮》，冊承天太后儀，侍中就席解劍脫履。

translations.literal: In the "Miscellaneous Rites," for the investiture of Empress Dowager Chengtian, the attendant-in-chief took his seat, removed his sword, and took off his shoes.
translations.idiomatic: In the Miscellaneous Rites, at the investiture of Empress Dowager Chengtian, the attendant-in-chief took his seat, removed his sword, and took off his shoes.

sentences.zh: 重熙五年尊號冊禮，皇帝服龍袞，北南臣僚並朝服，蓋遼制。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongxi, at the honorific-title investiture, the emperor wore dragon regalia; northern and southern officials all wore court dress—this was Liao custom.
translations.idiomatic: At the honorific-title investiture in the fifth year of Chongxi, the emperor wore dragon regalia and officials of both northern and southern courts wore court dress—this was Liao practice.

sentences.zh: 會同中，太后、北面臣僚國服；

translations.literal: During Huitong, the empress dowager and northern-bureau officials wore national dress;
translations.idiomatic: During the Huitong period, the empress dowager and northern-court officials wore Khitan national dress;

sentences.zh: 皇帝、南面臣僚漢服。

translations.literal: the emperor and southern-bureau officials wore Han dress.
translations.idiomatic: while the emperor and southern-court officials wore Chinese dress.

sentences.zh: 乾亨以後，大禮雖北面三品以上亦用漢服；

translations.literal: After Qianheng, even for great rites northern-bureau officials of third rank and above also used Han dress;
translations.idiomatic: After Qianheng, even at great rites northern-court officials of third rank and above wore Chinese dress;

sentences.zh: 重熙以後，大禮並漢服矣。

translations.literal: After Chongxi, great rites were entirely in Han dress.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongxi, great rites were conducted entirely in Chinese dress.

sentences.zh: 常朝仍遵會同之制。

translations.literal: Ordinary court audiences still followed the Huitong regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary court audiences still followed the Huitong regulations.

sentences.zh: 皇帝通天冠，諸祭還及冬至、朔日受朝、臨軒拜王公、元會、冬會服之。

translations.literal: The emperor wore the tongtian crown upon returning from sacrifices, and at winter solstice, new-moon audiences, hall audiences honoring princes and dukes, New Year's assembly, and winter assembly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore the tongtian crown when returning from sacrifices, and at the winter solstice, new-moon audiences, hall audiences honoring princes and dukes, the New Year's assembly, and the winter assembly.

sentences.zh: 冠加金博山，附蟬十二，首施珠翠。

translations.literal: The crown bore a gold Boshan peak, twelve cicada ornaments attached, and pearls and kingfisher feathers atop the head.
translations.idiomatic: The crown bore a gold Boshan peak, twelve attached cicada ornaments, and pearls and kingfisher feathers on the brow.

sentences.zh: 黑介幘，緌纓翠緌，玉若犀簪導。

translations.literal: Black inner cap, tassel cords and kingfisher tassels, jade or rhinoceros-horn hairpins guiding the crown.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a black inner cap with tassel cords and kingfisher tassels, secured by jade or rhinoceros-horn hairpins.

sentences.zh: 絳紗袍，白紗中單，褾領，朱襈裾，白裙襦，絳蔽膝，白假帶方心曲領。

translations.literal: Crimson gauze robe, white gauze undergarment, lapel collar, vermilion skirt hem, white skirt and jacket, crimson knee covers, white false belt with square heart and curved collar.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a crimson gauze robe over a white gauze undergarment, with lapel collar, vermilion skirt hem, white skirt and jacket, crimson knee covers, and a white false belt with square heart and curved collar.

sentences.zh: 其革帶佩劍綬，襪舄。

translations.literal: Leather belt, sword, pendant sash, socks, and shoes completed the ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: A leather belt, sword, pendant sash, socks, and shoes completed the ensemble.

sentences.zh: 若未加元服，則雙童髻，空頂，黑介幘，雙玉導，加寶飾。

translations.literal: If the coming-of-age ceremony had not yet been performed, he wore paired child topknots, bare crown, black inner cap, paired jade guides, and precious ornaments added.
translations.idiomatic: If he had not yet undergone the coming-of-age ceremony, he wore paired child topknots, a bare crown, a black inner cap, paired jade hairpins, and precious ornaments.

sentences.zh: 《元日上壽儀》，皇帝服通天冠，絳紗袍。

translations.literal: In the "New Year's Birthday Congratulations Rite," the emperor wore the tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rite of New Year's Birthday Congratulations, the emperor wore the tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 皇太子遠遊冠，謁廟還宮、元日、冬至朔日入朝服之。

translations.literal: The crown prince wore the yuanyou crown when returning from temple visits, and on New Year's Day and winter-solstice new-moon court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wore the yuanyou crown when returning from temple visits and on New Year's Day and the winter-solstice new-moon court audience.

sentences.zh: 三梁冠，加金附蟬九，首施珠翠。

translations.literal: A three-ridged crown with gold and nine attached cicadas; pearls and kingfisher feathers on the head.
translations.idiomatic: It was a three-ridged crown with gold and nine attached cicadas, with pearls and kingfisher feathers on the brow.

sentences.zh: 黑介幘，發纓翠緌，犀簪導。

translations.literal: Black inner cap, hair tassels and kingfisher cords, rhinoceros-horn hairpins guiding the crown.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a black inner cap with hair tassels and kingfisher cords, secured by rhinoceros-horn hairpins.

sentences.zh: 絳紗袍，白紗中單，皂領褾，襈裾，白裾襦，白假帶方心曲領，絳紗蔽膝。

translations.literal: Crimson gauze robe, white gauze undergarment, black collar and lapel, vermilion skirt hem, white skirt and jacket, white false belt with square heart and curved collar, crimson gauze knee covers.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a crimson gauze robe over a white gauze undergarment, with black collar and lapel, vermilion skirt hem, white skirt and jacket, white false belt with square heart and curved collar, and crimson gauze knee covers.

sentences.zh: 其革帶劍佩綬，襪舄與上同，後改用白襪、黑舄。

translations.literal: Leather belt, sword, pendant sash, socks, and shoes were the same as above; later white socks and black shoes were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The leather belt, sword, pendant sash, socks, and shoes matched the emperor's; later white socks and black shoes were adopted.

sentences.zh: 未冠，則雙童髻，空頂，黑介幘，雙玉導，加寶飾。

translations.literal: Before crowning, he wore paired child topknots, bare crown, black inner cap, paired jade guides, and precious ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Before his crowning, he wore paired child topknots, a bare crown, a black inner cap, paired jade hairpins, and precious ornaments.

sentences.zh: 《冊皇太子儀》，皇太子冠遠遊，服絳紗袍。

translations.literal: In the "Investiture of the Crown Prince Rite," the crown prince wore the yuanyou crown and crimson gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rite of Investiture of the Crown Prince, the crown prince wore the yuanyou crown and crimson gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 親王遠遊冠，陪祭朝饗、拜表、大事服之。

translations.literal: Imperial princes wore the yuanyou crown for accompanying sacrifices, court feasts, presenting memorials, and great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes wore the yuanyou crown when accompanying sacrifices, attending court feasts, presenting memorials, and on other great occasions.

sentences.zh: 冠三梁，加金附蟬。

translations.literal: The crown had three ridges, with gold and attached cicadas.
translations.idiomatic: The crown had three ridges with gold and attached cicadas.

sentences.zh: 黑介幘，青緌導。

translations.literal: Black inner cap, blue tassel guides.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a black inner cap with blue tassel guides.

sentences.zh: 絳紗單衣，白紗中單，皂領，襈裾，白裾襦。

translations.literal: Crimson gauze single garment, white gauze undergarment, black collar, vermilion skirt hem, white skirt and jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a crimson gauze outer garment over a white gauze undergarment, with black collar, vermilion skirt hem, and white skirt and jacket.

sentences.zh: 革帶鈎䚢，假帶曲領方心，絳紗蔽膝，襪舄，劍佩綬二品以上同。

translations.literal: Leather belt with hooks and plaques, false belt with curved collar and square heart, crimson gauze knee covers, socks and shoes; sword, pendant sash—same as second rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a leather belt with hooks and plaques, a false belt with curved collar and square heart, crimson gauze knee covers, socks and shoes, and sword and pendant sash as for second rank and above.

sentences.zh: 諸王遠遊冠，三梁，黑介幘，青緌。

translations.literal: Princes wore the yuanyou crown, three-ridged, with black inner cap and blue tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Princes wore the three-ridged yuanyou crown with a black inner cap and blue tassels.

sentences.zh: 三品以上進賢冠，三梁，寶飾。

translations.literal: Third rank and above wore the jinxian crown, three-ridged, with precious ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of third rank and above wore the three-ridged jinxian crown with precious ornaments.

sentences.zh: 五品以上進賢冠，二梁，金飾。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above wore the jinxian crown, two-ridged, with gold ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fifth rank and above wore the two-ridged jinxian crown with gold ornaments.

sentences.zh: 九品以上進賢冠，一梁，無飾。

translations.literal: Ninth rank and above wore the jinxian crown, one-ridged, without ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of ninth rank and above wore the one-ridged jinxian crown without ornaments.

sentences.zh: 七品以上去劍佩綬。

translations.literal: Seventh rank and above removed sword and pendant sash.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of seventh rank and above did without sword and pendant sash.

sentences.zh: 八品以下同公服。

translations.literal: Eighth rank and below followed official dress.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of eighth rank and below wore the same as official dress.

sentences.zh: 公服：《勘箭儀》，閣使公服，系履。

translations.literal: Official dress: in the "Arrow-Verification Rite," pavilion envoys wore official dress and tied on their shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Official dress: in the Arrow-Verification Rite, pavilion envoys wore official dress and tied on their shoes.

sentences.zh: 遼國常用公服矣。

translations.literal: The Liao state commonly used official dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao commonly wore official dress.

sentences.zh: 皇帝翼善冠，朔視朝用之。

translations.literal: The emperor wore the yishan crown for new-moon court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore the yishan crown for new-moon court audiences.

sentences.zh: 柘黃袍，九環帶，白練裙襦，六合靴。

translations.literal: Cudrania-yellow robe, nine-ring belt, white silk skirt and jacket, six-panel boots.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a cudrania-yellow robe, a nine-ring belt, a white silk skirt and jacket, and six-panel boots.

sentences.zh: 皇太子遠遊冠，五日常朝、元日、冬至受朝服。

translations.literal: The crown prince wore the yuanyou crown for weekday audiences, New Year's Day, and winter-solstice audiences.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wore the yuanyou crown for weekday audiences, New Year's Day, and the winter-solstice audience.

sentences.zh: 絳紗單衣，白裙襦，革帶，金鈎䚢，假帶方心，紛鞶囊，白䚢，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Crimson gauze single garment, white skirt and jacket, leather belt, gold hooks and plaques, false belt with square heart, patterned pouch, white plaques, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a crimson gauze outer garment, white skirt and jacket, leather belt with gold hooks and plaques, false belt with square heart, patterned pouch, white plaques, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 一品以下、五品以上。

translations.literal: Below first rank, fifth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: For officials below first rank and of fifth rank and above:

sentences.zh: 冠幘纓，簪導，謁見東宮及餘公事服之。

translations.literal: Cap with headcloth tassels and hairpin guides; worn for audiences with the Eastern Palace and other official business.
translations.idiomatic: They wore caps with headcloth tassels and hairpin guides when attending upon the Eastern Palace and on other official business.

sentences.zh: 絳紗單衣，白裙襦，帶鈎䚢，假帶方心，襪履，紛鞶囊。

translations.literal: Crimson gauze single garment, white skirt and jacket, belt with hooks and plaques, false belt with square heart, socks and shoes, patterned pouch.
translations.idiomatic: They wore crimson gauze outer garments, white skirts and jackets, belts with hooks and plaques, false belts with square heart, socks and shoes, and patterned pouches.

sentences.zh: 六品以下，冠幘纓，簪導，去紛鞶囊，餘並同。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below: cap with headcloth tassels and hairpin guides, without patterned pouch; the rest the same.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of sixth rank and below wore caps with headcloth tassels and hairpin guides but without the patterned pouch; otherwise the same.

sentences.zh: 常服：遼國謂之「穿執」。

translations.literal: Ordinary dress: the Liao state called it "chuan zhi."
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary dress: the Liao called it "chuan zhi."

sentences.zh: 起居禮臣僚穿執。

translations.literal: In the daily-audience rite, officials wore chuan zhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the daily-audience rite, officials wore chuan zhi.

sentences.zh: 言穿靴、執笏也。

translations.literal: That is to say, wearing boots and holding the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The term means wearing boots and holding the court tablet.

sentences.zh: 皇帝柘黃袍衫，折上頭巾，九環帶，六合靴，起自宇文氏。

translations.literal: The emperor wore cudrania-yellow robe and jacket, folded-up headcloth, nine-ring belt, and six-panel boots—originating with the Yuwen clan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore a cudrania-yellow robe and jacket, a folded-up headcloth, a nine-ring belt, and six-panel boots—a style originating with the Yuwen clan.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗貞觀已後，非元日、冬至受朝及大祭祀，皆常服而已。

translations.literal: After Emperor Taizong of Tang's Zhenguan reign, except for New Year's and winter-solstice audiences and great sacrifices, only ordinary dress was worn.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhenguan reign of Emperor Taizong of Tang, ordinary dress alone sufficed except for New Year's and winter-solstice audiences and great sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 皇太子進德冠，九琪，金飾，絳紗單衣，白裙襦，白襪，烏皮履。

translations.literal: The crown prince wore the jinde crown with nine qi and gold ornaments, crimson gauze single garment, white skirt and jacket, white socks, and black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wore the jinde crown with nine qi and gold ornaments, a crimson gauze outer garment, white skirt and jacket, white socks, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 五品以上，襆頭，亦曰折上巾，紫袍，牙笏，金玉帶。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above: futou, also called zheshangjin, purple robe, ivory tablet, gold-and-jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fifth rank and above wore the futou, also called the folded-up headcloth, with a purple robe, an ivory tablet, and a gold-and-jade belt.

sentences.zh: 文官佩手巾、算袋、刀子、礪石、金魚袋；

translations.literal: Civil officials wore handkerchief, abacus pouch, knife, whetstone, and gold fish pouch;
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials carried a handkerchief, abacus pouch, knife, whetstone, and gold fish pouch;

sentences.zh: 武官䩞鞢七事：佩刀、刀子、磨石、契真、噦厥、針筒、火石袋。

translations.literal: Military officials had seven xiedie items: waist sword, knife, whetstone, qizhen, yujue, needle case, and flint pouch.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials wore seven xiedie accoutrements: a waist sword, knife, whetstone, qizhen, yujue, needle case, and flint pouch.

sentences.zh: 烏皮六合靴。

translations.literal: Black leather six-panel boots.
translations.idiomatic: They wore black leather six-panel boots.

sentences.zh: 六品以下，襆頭，緋衣，木笏，銀帶，銀魚袋佩，靴同。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below: futou, scarlet robe, wooden tablet, silver belt, silver fish pouch worn, boots the same.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of sixth rank and below wore the futou, scarlet robe, wooden tablet, silver belt, and silver fish pouch, with the same boots.

sentences.zh: 八品九品，襆頭，綠袍，鍮石帶，靴同。

translations.literal: Eighth and ninth ranks: futou, green robe, cupronickel belt, boots the same.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the eighth and ninth ranks wore the futou, green robe, and cupronickel belt, with the same boots.
